newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan slams China's U.N. moves against Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan slams China's U.N. moves against Guatemala.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday condemned rival China for using its U.N. Security Council seat to pressure Guatemala and other Latin American countries that recognise Taipei rather than Beijing.

"We should altogether condemn communist China's acts of using its influence in the U.N. Security Council to interfere in the internal affairs of central and south American countries," said Foreign Ministry deputy spokesman Chen Yung-tso.

Chen said he knew little about a closed-door meeting at U.N. headquarters in New York on Wednesday between diplomats from Beijing and Guatemala. "We need further checks," Chen said without elaborating.
U.N. diplomats said China had requested the meeting in a bid to repair the effects of its controversial veto that barred U.N. observers from monitoring a Guatemalan peace pact.
Fourteen of 15 council members on Friday voted in support of sending 155 military observers to Guatemala to monitor U.N.-brokered peace pacts that ended a three-decade civil war.

China, using its council veto for the first time in 25 years, blocked the mission because of Guatemala's ties to Taiwan, its support of Taipei's drive for U.N. membership and its invitation to Taiwan's foreign minister to attend a December 29 peace accord signing ceremony.

Beijing, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, has tightened a diplomatic embargo around the island by stepping up pressure on the handful of countries that recognise its exiled Republic of China.
